title: Decouple synchronous IO and introduce async KV-shard controller
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Background: The continuous-batching path still contains synchronous I/O handoffs to the legacy KV layer. Those sync hops increase tail latency under bursty ingress and block runtime worker threads during compaction/flush. This ticket refactors the hotpath to decouple sync IO, introduce an async KV-shard controller that exposes non-blocking shard-level APIs, and replace direct blocking flushes with a compact flusher background worker.

Goals:
- Remove blocking IO from the request-facing batcher/slot allocator so worker threads never wait on shard-level compaction.
- Introduce a KV-shard controller with explicit async APIs: async_read, async_prefetch, async_flush_request, and shard_health_probe.
- Add a compact flusher supervisor that batches small flush requests, enforces circuit-breaker backoff, and exposes metrics.
- Preserve existing correctness (no lost KV entries) and provide compatibility shim for older components during rollout.

Out of scope:
- Full rewrite of KV storage backend (persisted on-disk format remains unchanged).
- Global re-sharding logic (this ticket only touches shard-local controller).

Expected benefits:
- Reduced p99 request latency from blocking flushes. Target: p99 decrease by 15% on mix workloads.
- Reduced tail variance under burst traffic and lower thread contention.
- Better observability into flush queue depth and per-shard backpressure.

Trade-offs & risks:
- Additional moving parts and state (controller state machine) increases code surface area. We'll mitigate via thorough unit/integration tests and a staged canary.
- Potential transient increased memory usage during staggered async flushes. We'll set conservative limits and OOM guards in the flusher supervisor.

Design notes and artifacts:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Async+KV+Shard+Controller+Design
- RFC: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1qWf-Async-KV-Controller-RFC
- Initial prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8421
- Benchmark harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/benchmarks/tree/main/kv-async-flusher

Rollout plan:
1) Implement controller and compatibility shim behind runtime feature flag (kv.async-controller=true).
2) Unit tests + integration tests that simulate shard compaction and concurrent reads.
3) Canary rollout on non-critical pool with traffic shaping (2% of traffic). Monitor per-shard flush-queue, p50/p95/p99 latency, and OOM alerts.
4) Gradual ramp: 2% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% over two weeks with ability to roll back flag.

Monitoring / Success metrics:
- Request p99 lowered by >=15% on canary pool (compared to baseline).
- KV flush queue length per-shard remains < 200 items 95% of time.
- No increase in per-host OOM incidents.
- CPU utilization delta < +5% across hosts.

Compatibility shim:
- Legacy components call sync APIs which will be forwarded to controller implementation that blocks only on a per-request Future with timeout (short-term to preserve correctness). During rollout, we will flip consumers to the native async APIs to remove blocking waits entirely.
acceptance_criteria: All request-facing threads do not perform blocking disk/compaction on hotpath (verified by thread-blocking profiler)
Integration test suite simulates compaction under load and shows no increase in failed requests
Feature flag enables safe rollout and full rollback without state loss
Benchmarks show p99 improvement >= 15% on representative workload
comments: 2026-03-01 Aisha Kapoor: Created ticket after spike showed 300ms tail spikes during compaction windows. Linked initial profiling traces: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/abc123/batcher-thread-blocking?orgId=1
2026-03-03 Li Chen: Completed prototype for async_read/async_flush_request. Observed 10% p99 improvement locally. Pushing PR for early feedback: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8421

2026-03-05 Marco Hernández (review): Design looks reasonable. Concern: how do we bound memory for outstanding async flushes? Suggest adding configurable per-shard inflight limit and a global circuit-breaker. Added as TODO in design doc.
2026-03-07 Li Chen: Implemented compact flusher supervisor with per-shard inflight cap and exponential backoff. Added metrics kv.shard.flush_queue, kv.shard.inflight_count, kv.flusher.backoff_events.

2026-03-09 QA: Integration test failed when simulating an aggressive flush storm (10k flush requests/sec) — observed degraded CPU and increased GC. Mitigation: throttle flush acceptance and prioritize eviction of long-tail sessions. Added test case to harness.

2026-03-11 Li Chen: Addressed QA findings, tuned backpressure thresholds, added gated rollout via kv.async-controller flag. Ready to open canary run request. PR updated: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8527
